channel.title: The Brussels Times
channel.description: Latest posts from The Brussels Times.

item.title: Foreign Minister Prévot expresses condolences after Kraków shooting
item.description: Anyone concerned about relatives or in need of assistance can contact the Belgian embassy in Warsaw.

item.title: Family members of Palestinians in Belgium affected by severe Gaza storms
item.description: The damage to personal belongings has exceeded €3 million as floods swept through Gaza on Friday night.

item.title: US ambassador to Belgium outraged by Brussels synagogue attack
item.description: Bill White visited the synagogue in Anderlecht on Saturday with Israel’s ambassador to Belgium, David Saranga, after the building was targeted in what White called a clear act of antisemitic vandalism.

item.title: Congo wants its human remains back. What will it take for Belgium to return them?
item.description: More than 500 human remains from the DRC, Rwanda and Burundi are still held in Belgium. Some in the AfricaMuseum, but most at the Royal Belgian Institute of Natural Sciences.

item.title: Dutch customs seize 1.7 million counterfeit Pokémon cards at Rotterdam Port
item.description: All the cards have been destroyed, customs officials report.

item.title: 'We cannot trust the US': The European lesson from America's midterm landslide
item.description: While Europeans may be relieved by the Democrats' midterm landslide, experts warn that it does not mean the transatlantic relationship is back to normal.

item.title: US voters in Belgium weigh in on midterm elections seen as referendum on Trump
item.description: According to polls, Democrats are expected to win at least one and potentially both bodies of Congress as Trump's approval rating is at an all-time low.

item.title: ‘Association without accession’: Why the EU is offering Canada ‘ever-closer’ partnership
item.description: "We can build a partnership that comes closer to membership than anything we have done before.”

item.title: Greenpeace criticises UN biodiversity summit
item.description: The summit held in Yerevan, Armenia was said not to have brought the action needed to halt nature loss.

item.title: Crypto exchange Binance loses €5.4 billion in hack
item.description: A hacker may have stolen €5.4 billion from the crypto trading platform Binance in what, if confirmed, could be the biggest crypto theft ever.

item.title: ‘Wait and see’: EU ambassador explains cautious approach to Israel’s crucial vote
item.description: “The EU looks forward to engaging with the next government on the basis of our longstanding relationship."

item.title: 'Driver, proceed at normal speed': The moments leading up to the deadly train crash in Spain
item.description: Audio recordings obtained by El País revealed how one train raced down the tracks at its maximum speed, unaware of the other one blocking the tracks just ahead.

item.title: Belgium chairs European Nuclear Alliance
item.description: The alliance brings together European countries who want to promote nuclear power besides renewable sources.

item.title: UK and EU Erasmus+ youth exchanges to start in mid-2027
item.description: While the previous Erasmus scheme was focused on university mobility exchanges, Erasmus+ allows shorter exchanges of a few days.

item.title: Death toll rises to 68 following high-speed rail crash near Madrid
item.description: At least 64 people were killed in a train crash on Wednesday morning in Urda, about 100 kilometres south of Madrid, a spokesperson for the Castile-La Mancha regional government said.

item.title: EU to introduce extra fee on small parcels coming into the bloc
item.description: The European Union will introduce a €2 handling fee on small parcels ordered outside of the bloc from 1 November.

item.title: Netherlands confirms non-participation in Eurovision Song Contest 2027
item.description: Despite the non-participation, broadcaster NOS will still show the contest in the Netherlands, including with Dutch commentary.

item.title: UK Prime Minister sets out red lines on free movement ahead of November EU summit
item.description: He suggested that Labour’s next election campaign, expected in 2029, could include a pledge to rejoin the EU.

item.title: Six Belgian cities among most tourist-oriented cities in the world
item.description: Bruges and five other Belgian cities also made it into the top 100 of the most tourist-oriented cities in the world, according to a study published by One Street Back.

item.title: Psoriasis Day aims to break down taboos around rare skin disease
item.description: Symptoms are often mistaken for irritation, thrush or an STI, delaying proper treatment. Campaigners say the taboo around intimate psoriasis has become a wider societal issue.
